part.text: The dataset includes records through 2026, and 2025 has crashes dated through December 31, so the requested years appear to be complete calendar years. I’m using the sum of `number_of_pedestrians_killed` per crash, grouped by crash year; I’ll show that same annual count as both bars and a line to make the year-to-year levels and trend readable.

input.command:
python3 -c 'exec("""import duckdb
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path

out = Path(\"out\")
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
df = duckdb.sql(\"\"\"SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM crash_date)::INT AS year,
       SUM(COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_killed, 0))::BIGINT AS pedestrian_deaths
FROM read_parquet(\"data/crashes.parquet\")
WHERE crash_date >= DATE \'2013-01-01\' AND crash_date < DATE \'2026-01-01\'
GROUP BY year ORDER BY year\"\"\").df()
expected = list(range(2013, 2026))
assert df[\"year\"].tolist() == expected, df
for i, chart_type in [(1, \"bar\"), (2, \"line\")]:
    csv = out / f\"values_{i}.csv\"
    png = out / f\"option_{i}.png\"
    df.to_csv(csv, index=False)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
    if chart_type == \"bar\":
        bars = ax.bar(df[\"year\"], df[\"pedestrian_deaths\"], color=\"#2878B5\", width=0.72)
        ax.bar_label(bars, padding=3, fontsize=8)
    else:
        ax.plot(df[\"year\"], df[\"pedestrian_deaths\"], color=\"#C44E52\", marker=\"o\", linewidth=2)
        for x, y in zip(df[\"year\"], df[\"pedestrian_deaths\"]):
            ax.annotate(str(y), (x, y), xytext=(0, 7), textcoords=\"offset points\", ha=\"center\", fontsize=8)
    ax.set(title=\"Pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes by year (2013–2025)\",
           xlabel=\"Crash year\", ylabel=\"Pedestrians killed (people)\")
    ax.set_xticks(expected)
    ax.set_ylim(0, max(df[\"pedestrian_deaths\"]) + 28)
    ax.grid(axis=\"y\", alpha=0.25)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(png, dpi=180, bbox_inches=\"tight\")
    plt.close(fig)
print(df.to_string(index=False))
print(\"Saved charts and CSVs in out/\")
""")'

+        ax.plot(
+            data["year"],

+            color="#C44E52",
+            marker="o",
+            linewidth=2,
+        )
+        for year, deaths in zip(data["year"], data["pedestrian_deaths"]):
+            ax.annotate(
+                str(deaths),
+                (year, deaths),
+                xytext=(0, 7),
+                textcoords="offset points",
+                ha="center",
+                fontsize=8,
+            )
+    ax.set(
+        title="Pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes by year (2013–2025)",

+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(out / f"option_{option_id}.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+print(data.to_string(index=False))
*** End Patch
